text:
ConocoPhillips barely moved today, up just 0.04%, as oil prices fell on easing Middle East tensions. Yesterday (October 28), oil had spiked on reports of potential U.S. strikes against Iran, but today's news of renewed peace negotiations reversed that fear premium. With U.S. crude dropping from recent highs, the stock has stabilized after swinging up sharply over the past two weeks—a $5.74 move from October 22 to 23 when geopolitical risk was highest.

The stock remains up 5.21% over two weeks, reflecting the oil market's volatility around Middle East conflict risk. The wide gap between world oil ($123/barrel) and U.S. oil ($103/barrel) also shows that global supply concerns persist, even if today's de-escalation headlines briefly eased the immediate threat.
